reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
There are 10 marbles in a bag: 5 red, and 5 blue.

Sue draws a marble from the bag at random. The marble is red.

She puts the marble back into the bag.

What is the probability that the next marble she draws at random is red?
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Color of Caps

[Image: A pie chart indicating 30% white caps, 25% green caps, 15% black caps, 10% blue caps, and 20% red caps.]

The pie chart shows the percentage of caps for sale at a sporting goods store. If there are 200 caps, what is the total number of caps that are either white or green?
reference_items.figure_description: A pie chart titled "Color of Caps" divided into five sectors: White (labeled "White 30%") occupying the top-left sector; Green (labeled "Green 25%") occupying the top-right quadrant; Red (labeled "Red 20%") occupying the bottom-right sector; Blue (labeled "Blue 10%") occupying a narrow sector at the bottom; and Black (labeled "Black 15%") occupying the sector between Blue and White on the lower left.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: A bowl contains 36 colored beads all of the same size: some blue, some green, some red, and the rest yellow. A bead is drawn from the bowl without looking. The probability that it is blue is 4/9. How many blue beads are in the bowl?
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: Sophie has a bag in which there are 16 marbles: 8 are red and 8 are black marbles. She draws 2 marbles from the bag and does not put them back. Both marbles are black. She then draws a third marble out of the bag. What can you say about the likely color of this third marble?

options.label: A
options.text: It is more likely to be red than black.

options.label: B
options.text: It is more likely to be black than red.

options.label: C
options.text: It is equally likely to be red or black.

options.label: D
options.text: You cannot tell if red or black is more likely.

reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The figure below shows a spinner with 24 sectors. When someone spins the arrow, it is equally likely to stop on any sector.

[Image: Spinner with 24 sectors]

1/8 of the sectors are blue, 1/24 are purple, 1/2 are orange, and 1/3 are red. If a person spins the arrow, on which color sector is the spinner LEAST likely to stop?
reference_items.figure_description: A circular spinner divided equally into 24 sectors by radial line segments from a central pivot point. An arrow is mounted at the center, pointing toward the sector at approximately the 1 o'clock position. The sectors are plain white and unlabeled.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The eleven chips shown below are placed in a bag and mixed.

[Image: Eleven numbered chips]

Chelsea draws one chip from the bag without looking. What is the probability that Chelsea draws a chip with a number that is a multiple of three?
reference_items.figure_description:
Eleven circular/oval chips arranged in two rows:
- Top row has 5 chips labeled with numbers: 2, 3, 5, 6, 8.
- Bottom row has 6 chips labeled with numbers: 10, 11, 12, 14, 18, 20.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A spinner, which is divided and labeled with purple, orange, green, blue, and red. The purple section takes up half of the spinner. The orange section takes up one fourth of the spinner. The green, blue, and red sections each take up one twelfth of the spinner.]

The spinner is for Steve's new game. Out of 600 spins, approximately how many times should he expect the arrow to land on the red sector?
reference_items.figure_description: A circular spinner with a central pivot dot and an arrow pointing toward the upper right. The circle is divided into five sectors by radius lines. A vertical diameter splits the circle: the entire right half is a single semicircle labeled 'Purple'. The top-left quadrant is labeled 'Orange'. The bottom-left quadrant is divided into three equal slices, labeled from top to bottom as 'Green', 'Blue', and 'Red'.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The smaller box contains 20 tickets numbered from 1 to 20. The larger box contains 100 tickets numbered from 1 to 100.

[Image: Two boxes containing tickets]

Without looking at them, you can pick a ticket from either box. Which box would give you the greater chance of picking out a ticket with the number 17 on it?

options.label: C
options.text: Both boxes would give the same chance

reference_items.figure_description: Two rectangular prism-shaped boxes drawn in perspective. The box on the left is smaller and labeled below as "20 tickets". The box on the right is noticeably larger and labeled below as "100 tickets".
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
There are 30 students in a class. The ratio of boys to girls in the class is 2:3.
How many boys are there in the class?

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
